html:
Alexander's conquests were the campaigns in which Alexander the Great of Macedon marched from the Aegean to the Indus and took the whole Persian Empire, between 334 and 323 BCE. He was 22 when he set out and 32 when he died.

The main steps:

  • 334 BCE: he crossed into Asia and won at the Granicus river.
  • 333 BCE: he beat the Persian king Darius III at Issus.
  • 332 to 331 BCE: he took Tyre after a long siege, then Egypt, where he founded Alexandria.
  • 331 BCE: he crushed Darius at Gaugamela and took Babylon, Susa and Persepolis, which he burned.
  • 329 to 327 BCE: hard years of fighting in Bactria and Sogdiana, in today's Afghanistan and Uzbekistan.
  • 326 BCE: he beat King Porus at the Hydaspes in the Punjab. His tired army then refused to go further east.

He came back through the deserts of southern Iran and died in Babylon in 323 BCE, without a clear heir. His generals fought over the empire for decades and split it into kingdoms, among them the Seleucids in Asia and the Ptolemies in Egypt.

The conquests began the Hellenistic age. Greek became a language of rule and trade from Egypt to Afghanistan, and Greek cities, coins, art and ideas spread across West and Central Asia, even reaching the Buddhist art of India.
sum: Alexander's conquests were the campaigns in which Alexander the Great of Macedon marched from the Aegean to the Indus and took the whole Persian Empire, between 334 and 323 BCE. He was 22 when he set out and 32 when he died.
